Defence Minister Rajanath Singh has said India will continue to act as a trusted net security
provider in the Indian Ocean region and the wider Indo-Pacific.
Addressing the 13th ASEAN Defence Minister's meeting plus, ADMM plus at Sibu in the
Philippines.
Mr Singh said India considers maritime security as an issue linked to the peace, security and
prosperity of this region.
He said, the theme for this year's ADMM Plus, Navigating Our Future Together, deeply resonates
with India's defence and foreign policies.
The minister added that India's emphasis on the rule of law, particularly the United
Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea and its advocacy for freedom of navigation
and overflight is not directed against any country.

Union Home Minister Amit Shah today spoke with the Chief Ministers of Andhra Pradesh,
Puducherry, Odisha and Chhattisgarh in the wake of Cyclone Ornab.
Mr. Shah assured them of every assistance to mitigate the hardship of the people in
the face of the disaster. In a social media post, the Minister said the NDRF and
DRF teams have sprung into action and are continuing rescue and relief operations on a war footing.
Mr. Shah added that an interministerial central team will soon be sent to these states to
assess the impact and further assistance required. He said the central government stands with
the people with resolute commitment. Meanwhile, Cyclonic Storm Ornabh, which weakened into
a deep repression of a north-coastal Andhra Pradesh and adjoining areas of South Odisha,
India, South Chhattisgarh and Northeast Telangana has further weakened into a depression.
It lay centered over South Chhattisgarh and adjoining South Odisha and moved nearly northwards
over the same region.
IMD said it is very likely to continue to move nearly northwards and weakened into
a well-marked low-pressure area over North Chhattisgarh and adjoining Northwest Odisha
around evening today.
The Metapartman said during the past 24 hours there has been widespread rainfall
activity over North Andhra Pradesh, Northeast Telangana, Chhattisgarh, Odisha, Jharkhand and
Gangetic West Bengal. The cyclone's impact is likely to continue over Andhra Pradesh for the
next 24 hours. Meanwhile, a low-pressure area over the South Andaman Sea is expected to intensify,
bringing light to moderate rainfall and thunderstorms to parts of coastal Andhra Pradesh
over the next two days. A report. The depression, a remnant of very severe cyclonic
next storm, Ornab over South Chathisgarh and adjoining South Odisha moved nearly northwards

Although Cyclone Ornab has weakened its impact is likely to continue another 24 hours, according
to the meteorological department, light to moderate rainfall is expected in several parts
of Andhra Pradesh today and tomorrow.
Meanwhile, a low-pressure area over the South Andaman Sea and adjoining areas is
likely to move west-northwestwards and intensify into a well-marked low-pressure
area within the next 24 hours.
Under its influence, light-to-moderate rainfall or thunderstorms are likely at isolated places
across coastal Andhra Pradesh over the next two days.
Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister Nara Chandrabhupnidhu has directed officials to work around the clock
until normancy is restored in a cyclone-affected areas.

Uttarakhand is experiencing cold conditions following snowfall at the Charatham shrines
and other higher altitude areas, along with intermittent rainfall in the plains,
including Dehradol. The meteorological department has issued a yellow alert for rainfall across
the state for the next two days. Snowfall is also likely in areas situated at elevations
of 3,200 meters and above a report.
The season's first snowfall has been recorded at Kedarnath Dham and Gangotri Dham. Swami
Raghivendraji Maharaj said that the snowfall has made the shrines surrounding picturesque
and devotees visiting the shrine are enjoying the scenic beauty at Gangotri Dham. The administration
has appealed to devotees to wear warm clothes, take care of their health, and follow the
guidelines issued by the administration and police. According to the Met Department,
heavy rainfall is likely at isolated places in Pithoragar, Bageshwar, Nainital and Champa
with districts tomorrow. Light to moderate, rainfall is expected in the Healy district
until the 2nd of November, while snowfall is likely in higher altitude areas. The administration
has urged tourists, devotees and local residents to stay updated on weather conditions and
exercise caution during adverse weather. Sakshi Singh, Akashwani news, Theradun.
Welcome back to the midday news.
The National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority NPPA has released a list of 543 brands of anti-cancer
medicines with their revised maximum retail price MRP.
The revised MRPs will be effective from the 9th of next month.
The revised price list reflects the information submitted by companies up to the 27th of
this month and it will be updated as and when manufacturers submit their revised prices of
non-sheduled anti-cancer drugs.
According to the official release by the Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers, several key
anti-cancer brands have seen steep price drops.
The revision in prices comes amid NPPA's announcement on 17 October of trade margin
rationalization for 137 non-sheduled anti-cancer drugs in the public interest, aimed
at curbing excessive trade margins, making cancer treatment more affordable and improving
access to anti-cancer medicines.
Chief Economic Advisor Dr. V. Ananta Nageshwaran today highlighted that India's real GDP grew
by 7.8% in the first quarter of 2026-2027, supported by strong manufacturing and investment.
Dr. Nageshwaran also noted that manufacturing gross value added stood at 9.2% in the first
quarter of 2026-27 and merchandise export growth during April to September this year was 18.5%.
He made these remarks in New Delhi while addressing the inaugural session of the ISID IDRA
4th National Conference on India's Industrial Transformation Reimagining
Industrial Strategy Amidst Global Economic Uncertainty.
We are approaching this situation from a position of resilience and strength because
very few economies have achieved post-COVID what we have done. 7% plus real GDP growth
and especially this year the first quarter numbers are well distributed across all expenditure
components of GDP and also on the supply side we have done well with capital goods
output growth and manufacturing gross value added 9.2% year on year in the first quarter
and overall capital formation is showing signs of picking up even in the private sector
are taking over the baton from the public sector over the last several years.
Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal has said India's proposed trade deal with
the United States will protect farmers' interests and give India a competitive advantage.
Addressing the fourth National Conference on India's Industrial Transformation in
New Delhi today, Mr Goyal said the trade agreements will be fair, equitable and balanced.
The US trade deal is sometimes sought to be politicized by a few elements, but I have
the courage of conviction to announce boldly that the US trade deal, once details are out,
the people of India will celebrate that not a single sensitive interest of our farmers
or any stakeholder has been compromised.
India has called for greater representation of women in the armed forces, stating that
their participation can strengthen the protection of women and girls affected by conflicts and
advance the United Nations Women, Peace and Security WPS agenda.
Speaking at the UN Security Council's open debate on WPS yesterday, India's permanent
representative B. Harish cited a UN report stating that 750 million women and girls
live within 50 km of conflict zones. He also highlighted that verified cases of
conflict-related sexual violence had more than doubled in a year.
25 years since the adoption of Resolution 1325 is an apt moment to reflect on the path
throbbing and the path forward. The SGS report conveys urgency of addressing the
issue. Over 750 million women and girls live within 50 kilometers of conflict.
Verified cases of conflict-related sexual violence have more than doubled in a year.
SRSG pattern in her report had underlined how sexual violence has become a
political weapon in a world increasingly marked by conflicts.

of Resolution 1325, India supports UN's efforts to achieve full gender parity across its workforce
East Wales Central Elections Committee Chair Justice Noam Solberg has directed Shin Bet
Chief David Zini to investigate allegations of foreign interference in the elections seeking
findings within a week.
The move follows Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's claims of bribery, threats
and voter fraud involving Arab parties. The allegations remain unverified. The partial
election results show Netanyahu-led bloc holds 53 seats, 8 shots of the 61 needed for a majority.
In Hockey, India will take on China in the second league match of the Men's Asian
Champions Trophy 2026 today. The match is scheduled to begin at 7pm. The championship is presently
on at Olympian Sujit Hockey Stadium in Jalandhar. At the highly-opened badminton in 2026,
India's VV Sindhu, Malvika Bansord and Unnati Huda have advanced to the round of 16 after winning
their opening round matches. Sindhu defeated the UAE's Prakriti Bharat, 21-10, 21-10 in 28 minutes,
while Malvika recovered from a game down to beat compatriot Devika Sihag.
